cells.title: Grade concept freshness from anchors and git, with seed and confirm verbs
cells.action: Add a freshness grade to the knowledge bundle (D3 27ad96a5, D8 4148025d). New module verbs/knowledge/freshness.rs exports one reader `grade_concept(root, concept) -> Grade { grade: confirmed|suspect|orphan|unverified, verified_at: Option<String>, verified_commit: Option<String>, anchors: Vec<String>, changed: Vec<String>, reason: Option<String> }` over three new frontmatter fields under `bee`: `anchors` (flat list of repo-relative paths), `verified_at` (ISO date) and `verified_commit` (full sha). Grade rule, exactly: `orphan` when any anchor path is missing on disk; else `unverified` when there are no anchors, or verified_commit is absent or does not resolve (`git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` fails), or git is unavailable — `reason` names which; else `suspect` when any anchor was changed by a commit in `verified_commit..HEAD` that did NOT also touch the concept file (use `git log --format=%H <verified_commit>..HEAD -- <anchor>` and, for each such commit, `git show --name-only --format= <sha>` to test whether the concept path is in it); else `confirmed`. Shell to git through verbs/worktree/git.rs `run_git` (anchor: `pub(crate) fn run_git(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> GitOut {`). In check.rs, after the existing profile pass, grade every concept under areas/ and patterns/ (never work/, never index.md) and emit: one summary line `freshness: <n> confirmed, <n> suspect, <n> orphan, <n> unverified` in text, a `freshness` object in --json with those counts plus `rows: [{path, grade, verified_at, verified_commit, changed, reason}]`, and one profile WARNING row per suspect concept (code `stale_anchor`, message naming the changed anchor paths and the remedy `bee knowledge confirm --id <id>`) and per orphan concept (code `orphan_anchor`, naming the missing path). Unverified is counted, never warned. Two new verbs routed in routing.rs (anchor: `"check" => run_check(flags, json, pre_json, t0),`) and declared in generated/registry_payload.json as `{name, invoke, description}` rows like the existing `knowledge.check` row (the registry tests fail on an undeclared served verb; edit the JSON by a round-trip that keeps its byte format): `bee knowledge anchors seed [--dry-run]` walks areas/ and patterns/, and for every concept with NO `bee.anchors` key collects the backticked repo-relative paths in its body that exist on disk (same backtick-path shape dangling_source_candidate accepts; skip paths under .bee/ and docs/), writes them as `bee.anchors` through the canonical emitter (frontmatter.rs `emit_scalar`/`is_plain_safe` — a seeded file must report zero not_canonical), leaves `verified_*` unset, and prints per-file counts plus how many concepts got zero anchors; `bee knowledge confirm --id <bee.id>` refuses an unknown id or a concept with no anchors, otherwise sets `bee.verified_at` to today (UTC, ISO date) and `bee.verified_commit` to the current HEAD sha and re-emits canonically. Tests red-first in knowledge/tests.rs on a fixture repo with real git commits: each of the four grades; an anchor changed in a commit that also touched the concept grades confirmed; an unknown verified_commit grades unverified with a reason; seed writes anchors only where absent and the file stays canonical; confirm stamps both fields and refuses an unknown id; check's --json carries the freshness object and the stale_anchor / orphan_anchor rows.
cells.verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee -- knowledge registry

truths: grade_concept returns confirmed, suspect, orphan or unverified by the rule in plan.md Approach, and never confirmed when git is unavailable
an anchor changed in a commit that also touched the concept file does not make the concept suspect
bee knowledge check prints the freshness count line, carries the freshness object in --json, and emits stale_anchor and orphan_anchor warnings
bee knowledge anchors seed writes bee.anchors only to concepts without one and keeps every written file canonical
bee knowledge confirm --id stamps verified_at and verified_commit and refuses an unknown id

artifacts.substantive: grade_concept reader plus the seed and confirm verbs

key_links: check.rs calls grade_concept for every areas/ and patterns/ concept
routing.rs serves anchors seed and confirm
prohibitions: Do not grade or seed anything under docs/knowledge/work/
Do not change any existing finding code or its wording
open_choices: Keep the seed and confirm verbs in freshness.rs instead of author.rs

cells.title: Print the grade wherever a concept is read
cells.action: Make the freshness grade visible at every pull point (D1 2b11f025, D3 27ad96a5), using only `grade_concept` from kfm-1 — never a second grading rule. search.rs: `SearchHit` (anchor: `pub(crate) struct SearchHit {`) gains grade, verified_at and verified_commit; the text line becomes `<path> — <title> — [<grade> @ <verified_at or never>] — <why>` and the JSON row (anchor: `row.insert("why".into(), Value::String(hit.why.clone()));`) gains `grade`, `verified_at`, `verified_commit`. author.rs `run_show` prints a `freshness:` line after the metadata and adds the same three keys to its JSON. context.rs: every manifest entry (ranks 1-5) carries `grade` and `verified_at`; a suspect or orphan entry's inclusion reason ends with ` (grade: suspect — <first changed anchor>)` so the agent sees it in the reason column; ranking is unchanged. session_preamble: render.rs `knowledge_context_lines` (anchor: `pub(crate) fn knowledge_context_lines(root: &Path, record: &JMap) -> Vec<String> {`) adds ONE line `- knowledge: <n> confirmed, <m> suspect, <k> orphan, <u> unverified — suspect first: bee knowledge check` computed over areas/ and patterns/; the line is omitted when the bundle is absent, and the preamble byte budget must not grow by more than that one line (existing budget tests stay green). Tests red-first: a search row and a show output carry the grade of a fixture concept in each of two grades; a context manifest entry carries grade and the suspect reason suffix; the preamble line counts a fixture bundle correctly and is absent without a bundle.

cells.title: Refuse a cap that leaves an anchored concept unconfirmed
cells.action: Add check (d) to the cap-time sync door (D4 e7e80d78) in sync_door.rs `sync_refusal` (anchor: `pub(crate) fn sync_refusal(root: &Path, cell: &Map<String, Value>, touched: &[String]) -> Option<String> {`), after check (c): for every areas/ or patterns/ concept whose `bee.anchors` (normalized with normalize_cell_path) intersects `touched`, the cap passes when the concept's own path is in `touched` (edited or confirmed in this cell's commit) OR `grade_concept` returns confirmed; otherwise refuse with `capCell: SYNC_DOOR — cell "<id>" touches <paths> anchored by knowledge concept(s) <concept paths> that are not re-confirmed. FIX: bee knowledge confirm --id <bee.id> (then commit the concept with the cell), edit the concept, or pass --sync-ack "<reason>" to cap anyway (the reason is recorded on trace.sync_ack and trace.deviations).` The existing `--sync-ack` escape in handlers_close.rs covers (d) with no new flag. A bundle with no concepts, or a repo without docs/knowledge/, makes (d) a no-op. In skills/bee-swarming/SKILL.md, under the worker contract ("Execute"), add the step: before committing, run `bee knowledge check --json` and for every suspect concept anchored by a file you changed, either fix the concept or run `bee knowledge confirm --id <id>`, and commit the concept file with the cell — one sentence, cited to this feature's CONTEXT.md D4, no second copy of the grade rule. Because skills/ is hashed by the release manifest, run `bee dev regen` and include the regenerated manifest. Tests red-first in cells/tests.rs with a fixture repo and bundle: a cap touching an anchored file with the concept unconfirmed refuses and names the concept and the confirm remedy; the same cap passes when the concept file is in the touched set; passes after `knowledge confirm` with the concept committed; passes with --sync-ack and records the reason; a touched file anchored by no concept passes untouched.
cells.verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee -- cells::tests::sync && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check

cells.title: Write the homes rule and re-confirm step, and seed bee's own anchors
cells.action: Document the mechanic and apply it to bee's bundle (D2 93e1001d, D7 6a502ad0, D8 4148025d). Write one new concept docs/knowledge/areas/okf-profile/freshness-and-document-homes.md through `bee knowledge new --type <the area concept type used by the sibling files> --area okf-profile` and then edit its body: (1) the document homes rule — the four kinds that live in docs/knowledge (vision, glossary, area map with boundaries and invariants, decisions, patterns) and the three that live in code (verify features and tests, generated contracts, runnable runbooks), with the sentence that every area entry anchors to at least one code file or verify feature; (2) the three fields `bee.anchors`, `bee.verified_at`, `bee.verified_commit` and the grade rule, cited from plan.md Approach by pointer, not copied; (3) the cap re-confirm step and the `--sync-ack` escape; (4) the pull-rate measure and what a flat rate means (the lean layer is deleted next); (5) a Pointers section naming freshness.rs, sync_door.rs, report.rs and this feature's CONTEXT.md; and set its own `bee.anchors` to those three Rust files. Link it from okf-profile/overview.md (one bullet) and regenerate indexes with `bee knowledge index`. In skills/bee-capturing/SKILL.md add, in the capture discipline, one short paragraph: when a captured behaviour change touches a file an area concept anchors, re-confirm or edit that concept (`bee knowledge confirm --id`), and new area entries carry `bee.anchors` — cite the new concept by path, no second copy of the rule; because skills/ is hashed, run `bee dev regen` and include the regenerated manifest. Then run `bee knowledge anchors seed` once over areas/ and patterns/ (kfm-1's verb; kfm-4 has already moved work/ out) and commit the seeded frontmatter; record in the cap report how many concepts received anchors and how many got none. Finish with `bee knowledge check` (0 OKF errors, 0 profile errors; the stale_anchor warnings it now prints are expected and are the next feature's input — quote the freshness count line in the cap) and `bee dev release-manifest --check`.
